annotation.title_clean: Who Is Responsible? Self-Adaptation Under Multiple Concurrent Failures With Unknown Faults in Complex Robotic Systems
annotation.title_en: Who Is Responsible? Self-Adaptation Under Multiple Concurrent Failures With Unknown Faults in Complex Robotic Systems
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Wiedholz, A.; Paintner, R.; Hoffmann, A.; Huber, T.
annotation.summary_en: Technical robotics paper presenting a ROS2 MAPE-K self-adaptation approach with a DSL and live dependency graph for root-cause analysis and strategy ranking under multiple concurrent, cascading failures. Evaluated on underwater robot and perception scenarios. "Responsibility" refers to faulty components, not legal governance.
key_provisions_or_claims: ROS2 self-adaptation based on MAPE-K handles multiple concurrent failures with differing criticality
DSL lets designers specify failure patterns, criticality levels and multiple adaptation strategies
Live dependency graph enables lightweight root-cause analysis
Self-optimizing component learns strategy success probabilities
Performance comparable to baselines for sequential failures; open-source code
